items.title: Aligning MLLMs with the Latent Structure of Human Cognition via Behavior-Derived Semantic Dimensions
items.abstract: This paper proposes a framework to align Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with human cognitive structures. It achieves this by using a behavior-derived semantic space and converting human similarity judgments into dimension-grounded linguistic rationales. This method enables MLLMs to learn not only correct answers but also justifications consistent with human decision-making criteria, improving their alignment with human cognition.
items.figure_caption: Overview of triplet-level semantic dimension attribution. (a) Human similarity judgements are collected via crowdsourcing. Then learning a representational embedding space via SPoSE yields the multidimensional mental representations of natural objects. (b) For one triplet, we compute the original softmax probability based on the entire representational embedding for all pairs. We then iteratively prune each dimension from the representational embedding space and compute the changes in softmax probabilities relative to those obtained with the full embedding as the relevance score for that dimension. By sorting these relevance scores in descending order, we establish a hierarchical ranking of dimensional importance. The top-1 dimension yielding the maximum probability change is regarded as the most salient semantic dimension driving the human decision-making.

items.title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces TradeWar, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in multi-turn trade negotiations by grounding dialogues in actual policy execution and economic outcomes. The core contribution is the TradeWar benchmark itself, which simulates trade policies and assesses their economic impact, and the TACTIC agent, which learns to negotiate effectively by adapting its strategy based on past experiences and opponent behavior without retraining the LLM.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Illustrative negotiation in TradeWar. Two countries bargain over reciprocal cobalt, machinery, and tariff terms; their dialogue-level agreement remains provisional until grounding, validation, and bilateral signing. Country A, a machinery exporter seeking cobalt, negotiates with Country B, a cobalt exporter seeking machinery. They agree on reciprocal supply shares and an import tariff, subject to grounding, validation, and bilateral signing.

items.title: ACCT: Asymmetric Cross-LLM Context Transfer
items.abstract: This paper introduces ACCT, a method for efficiently reusing context computation across different-sized language models. ACCT transforms the KV cache from a larger source model into a sparse representation that a smaller target model can directly use. This significantly reduces redundant computation when switching between models, decoupling context processing from downstream inference.
items.figure_caption: ACCT combines Cartographer selection, Allocator budgeting, and Compiler conversion to transfer source KV into sparse target KV for inference without context re-encoding.

items.title: Know When the Equation Is Wrong: Structural Uncertainty for LLM-Guided Symbolic Regression under Extrapolation
items.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of uncertainty in LLM-guided symbolic regression, particularly when extrapolating beyond observed data. The core method, LLM-SR-UQ, retains multiple plausible equation structures and quantifies uncertainty by measuring their disagreement. This structural uncertainty allows for more robust prediction intervals that widen appropriately when extrapolation is unreliable, improving coverage.

items.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
items.abstract: Latent Sparse Attention (LSA) addresses the quadratic cost of full attention for ultra-long contexts by hierarchically clustering keys in a learned latent space. Queries then score these clusters, significantly reducing computation for prefill, decoding, and training. This method maintains accuracy at scale and can be applied via distillation (D-LSA) or native training (N-LSA).
items.figure_caption: D-LSA and N-LSA overview. Top: one attention layer. The keys are pooled and clustered into buckets. A query ( ) scores the bucket centroids ( ) and attends only to the selected long-range keys (plus sink and window). Bottom: accuracy and performance (P: prefill, D: decode, T: training) for both D-LSA and N-LSA. D-LSA is shown with flat search. Its subquadratic variant, D-LSA (Tree), follows a similar trend (Figure 5 ).

items.title: Prune Gradually, Adapt Sparsely: Efficient Pruning of Large Language Models at Extreme Sparsity
items.abstract: This paper proposes ETAPS, a method for efficiently pruning large language models to achieve extreme sparsity without significant quality degradation. ETAPS gradually tightens a global sparsity constraint in stages, allowing a sparse delta to adapt and compensate for removed weights. This approach avoids the high memory costs of end-to-end mask optimization while outperforming existing methods in quality at high sparsity levels.

items.title: RECAST: REconstruction of Chain-of-Thought via Auditable Structured Traces
items.abstract: This paper introduces RECAST, a novel method for reconstructing the internal reasoning process (Chain-of-Thought) of large language models when their intermediate steps are hidden. Unlike prior methods that rely on visible reasoning traces, RECAST reconstructs the CoT by conditioning a decoder on the question and the model's final answer. This approach allows for auditing and understanding the reasoning of closed-source models, overcoming limitations of existing techniques.

items.title: ReX-GG: a LLM Ensemble Pipeline for Relation-extraction and Graph Generation
items.abstract: This paper introduces ReX-GG, a lightweight LLM ensemble pipeline for relation extraction and graph generation. It utilizes JSON-structured outputs and anonymous peer-review ranking to mitigate hallucinations and single-model failures, producing interactive, color-coded causal graphs from scientific articles. The core contribution is a customizable, efficient ensemble that balances performance and output control.
items.figure_caption: Schematic representation of the pipeline presented in the paper: a text file is fed to the LLM ensemble, where relation extraction is performed, and the best output is decided through anonymous peer-ranking; the extracted relation triplets iterate through an embedding model to improve graph structure and assimilate nodes with semantic similarity. The final result is a causal graph in HTML format.

items.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
items.abstract: This paper audits six LLMs to see if they provide consistent smoking cessation advice across different user personas. The core method involves posing the same four questions to twelve distinct personas, revealing that LLMs tailor advice based on user characteristics like age and perceived expertise. The key contribution is demonstrating significant persona-dependent variation in advice, particularly regarding the mention of FDA-approved medications, and proposing a system prompt intervention to ensure factual consistency.

items.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
items.abstract: This paper introduces SecPO, a novel adversarial training method for prompt injection security. It proposes a theoretically grounded loss function that approximates an ideal, injection-invariant reference model. Combined with an efficient adversarial training pipeline that generates strong injected inputs, SecPO significantly reduces attack success rates against state-of-the-art models.

items.title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer
items.abstract: This paper introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), a novel subquadratic sparse attention mechanism designed to overcome the quadratic scaling bottleneck in LLMs. ZHA achieves this by employing a hierarchical, tree-structured indexer that recursively compresses key summaries, allowing queries to efficiently retrieve relevant keys in a top-down traversal. This approach leads to sublinear scaling in sequence length for both routing and attention computation, enabling LLMs to handle longer contexts more effectively.
items.figure_caption: Figure 11 : Dense top- p p set size for individual query heads in Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, using the same six-book cohort and thresholds as Figure 1 . Rows identify full-attention layers and columns identify query heads, with zero-based indices. Each panel averages only across books. All panels share logarithmic axis limits; colors denote p p and the dotted black line gives the p = 1 p=1 reference.

items.title: Whose Values, Which Contexts, and What Signals? Grounding Cultural Value Alignment with Re3Culture
items.abstract: This paper introduces Re3Culture, a large-scale dataset designed to ground cultural value alignment in real human evidence. It addresses key questions about whose values to represent, where to observe them, and what signals reveal them, by collecting data from representative communities in realistic scenarios and analyzing revealed value signals. The contribution lies in providing a robust, evidence-based foundation for developing AI systems that align with diverse human cultural values.
items.figure_caption: Overview of our research framework and Re 3 Culture dataset. Top: three fundamental questions for grounding cultural value alignment in human data; Bottom: Re 3 Culture supports investigation of these questions by linking demographically sampled community members, realistic and culturally sensitive scenarios, and explicit value reasoning with contextual responses.

items.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space (LARC) to improve multimodal models' reasoning capabilities for image generation. LARC bridges the gap between discrete language reasoning and continuous image generation by performing reasoning directly on continuous latent representations. This approach aims to enable test-time scaling and fine-grained control, overcoming limitations of existing methods.
items.figure_caption: Test-time scaling. We investigate the effect of the number of latent during test-time. Under controlled experiments, LARC performs remarkable test-time scaling behavior , outperforming the best-of-N sampling on image generation [ 1 ] , image editing [ 27 ] , and visual reasoning [ 75 ] tasks.

items.title: What Standard Evaluations Hide About Detectors of Hijacked LLM Agents: Rare Attacks, Unseen Tools and Benchmark Transfer
items.abstract: This paper reveals that standard evaluations of LLM agent hijacking detectors are misleading due to their consistent, high attack rates and lack of diverse data. The core method involves testing existing detectors on benchmarks with varied attack rates and tool coverage, demonstrating that their performance significantly degrades when faced with rare attacks or unseen tools. The main contribution is highlighting the limitations of current evaluation practices and showing how detector effectiveness is overestimated, urging for more robust and realistic testing methodologies.

items.title: Asynchronous Flow Map Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces asynchronous flow map language models (aFMLMs) to enable one-step parallel token prediction by incorporating an ordering. The core method learns "flow maps" that define a tokenwise time schedule, controlling denoising progress and internalizing this order into hidden computations. This allows for generating all tokens simultaneously in a single forward pass, a significant contribution for parallel language modeling.

items.title: Completeness and Cost of Retrieval Structures for Multi-Tool Requests in LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper investigates retrieval structures for LLM agents handling multi-tool requests, which often fail if even one required tool is missed. The authors compare six retrieval methods on multi-tool testbeds, measuring their ability to retrieve all necessary tools (completeness@k) and their associated computational costs. Their key contribution is demonstrating that existing retrieval methods perform poorly on multi-tool requests, especially those requiring many tools, and highlighting the need for specialized structures.

items.title: How Much Can Tool Calls Reveal About You? Privacy Leakage from Tool-Call Traces
items.abstract: This paper investigates the privacy risks associated with LLM agents interacting with external tools via tool-call traces. The authors introduce PrivacyTrace, a benchmark to study user-profile inference from these traces, finding that attackers can achieve a significant success rate in inferring user attributes. Their work highlights that tool arguments and returned results are key information sources, and cross-session trace linking amplifies this risk.
items.figure_caption: Tool-call traces as a privacy side channel. In this example, geocoding results and patterns in requested travel times and transport modes may support inferences about the user’s location, health condition, and religious affiliation.

items.title: Stepwise-Querying: Distilling Reasoning without Access to Teacher Chain-of-Thought
items.abstract: This paper introduces Stepwise Querying, a method to distill reasoning from black-box large language models without direct access to their internal thought processes. By posing independent queries about intermediate steps, validity, and corrections, it generates richer supervision signals for training smaller student models. This approach significantly outperforms existing methods on mathematical and code reasoning tasks.

items.title: AI evaluators favor job applications written by certain AI models, independent of candidate quality
items.abstract: This paper introduces a framework to audit AI-driven job application screening. It reveals that AI evaluators exhibit a consistent preference for applications written by specific AI models, independent of the candidate's actual qualifications. This "generative preference hierarchy" can disadvantage certain models and introduce bias, with significant implications for fair hiring practices.

items.title: AutoAnalysis: An automated, self-updating meta-analysis of human-AI collaboration
items.abstract: This paper introduces AutoAnalysis, an automated system for continuously updating meta-analyses on human-AI collaboration. Its core method involves synthesizing empirical evidence to provide clear guidance on optimal human-AI teaming strategies. The key contribution is a dynamic, self-updating framework that addresses the limitations of manual meta-analyses, offering timely insights into when human-AI combinations outperform humans alone, but are generally outperformed by the superior individual agent.

papers.figure_caption: D-LSA and N-LSA overview. Top: one attention layer. The keys are pooled and clustered into buckets. A query ( ) scores the bucket centroids ( ) and attends only to the selected long-range keys (plus sink and window). Bottom: accuracy and performance (P: prefill, D: decode, T: training) for both D-LSA and N-LSA. D-LSA is shown with flat search. Its subquadratic variant, D-LSA (Tree), follows a similar trend (Figure 5 ).

papers.title: Prune Gradually, Adapt Sparsely: Efficient Pruning of Large Language Models at Extreme Sparsity
papers.abstract: This paper proposes ETAPS, a method for efficiently pruning large language models to achieve extreme sparsity without significant quality degradation. ETAPS gradually tightens a global sparsity constraint in stages, allowing a sparse delta to adapt and compensate for removed weights. This approach avoids the high memory costs of end-to-end mask optimization while outperforming existing methods in quality at high sparsity levels.

papers.title: RECAST: REconstruction of Chain-of-Thought via Auditable Structured Traces
papers.abstract: This paper introduces RECAST, a novel method for reconstructing the internal reasoning process (Chain-of-Thought) of large language models when their intermediate steps are hidden. Unlike prior methods that rely on visible reasoning traces, RECAST reconstructs the CoT by conditioning a decoder on the question and the model's final answer. This approach allows for auditing and understanding the reasoning of closed-source models, overcoming limitations of existing techniques.

papers.title: ReX-GG: a LLM Ensemble Pipeline for Relation-extraction and Graph Generation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ReX-GG, a lightweight LLM ensemble pipeline for relation extraction and graph generation. It utilizes JSON-structured outputs and anonymous peer-review ranking to mitigate hallucinations and single-model failures, producing interactive, color-coded causal graphs from scientific articles. The core contribution is a customizable, efficient ensemble that balances performance and output control.
papers.figure_caption: Schematic representation of the pipeline presented in the paper: a text file is fed to the LLM ensemble, where relation extraction is performed, and the best output is decided through anonymous peer-ranking; the extracted relation triplets iterate through an embedding model to improve graph structure and assimilate nodes with semantic similarity. The final result is a causal graph in HTML format.

papers.title: Same Question, Different Answers: Auditing Persona-Dependent Variation in Six LLMs on Smoking-Cessation Advice
papers.abstract: This paper audits six LLMs to see if they provide consistent smoking cessation advice across different user personas. The core method involves posing the same four questions to twelve distinct personas, revealing that LLMs tailor advice based on user characteristics like age and perceived expertise. The key contribution is demonstrating significant persona-dependent variation in advice, particularly regarding the mention of FDA-approved medications, and proposing a system prompt intervention to ensure factual consistency.

papers.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SecPO, a novel adversarial training method for prompt injection security. It proposes a theoretically grounded loss function that approximates an ideal, injection-invariant reference model. Combined with an efficient adversarial training pipeline that generates strong injected inputs, SecPO significantly reduces attack success rates against state-of-the-art models.

papers.title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA), a novel subquadratic sparse attention mechanism designed to overcome the quadratic scaling bottleneck in LLMs. ZHA achieves this by employing a hierarchical, tree-structured indexer that recursively compresses key summaries, allowing queries to efficiently retrieve relevant keys in a top-down traversal. This approach leads to sublinear scaling in sequence length for both routing and attention computation, enabling LLMs to handle longer contexts more effectively.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 11 : Dense top- p p set size for individual query heads in Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, using the same six-book cohort and thresholds as Figure 1 . Rows identify full-attention layers and columns identify query heads, with zero-based indices. Each panel averages only across books. All panels share logarithmic axis limits; colors denote p p and the dotted black line gives the p = 1 p=1 reference.

papers.title: Whose Values, Which Contexts, and What Signals? Grounding Cultural Value Alignment with Re3Culture
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Re3Culture, a large-scale dataset designed to ground cultural value alignment in real human evidence. It addresses key questions about whose values to represent, where to observe them, and what signals reveal them, by collecting data from representative communities in realistic scenarios and analyzing revealed value signals. The contribution lies in providing a robust, evidence-based foundation for developing AI systems that align with diverse human cultural values.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of our research framework and Re 3 Culture dataset. Top: three fundamental questions for grounding cultural value alignment in human data; Bottom: Re 3 Culture supports investigation of these questions by linking demographically sampled community members, realistic and culturally sensitive scenarios, and explicit value reasoning with contextual responses.

papers.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space (LARC) to improve multimodal models' reasoning capabilities for image generation. LARC bridges the gap between discrete language reasoning and continuous image generation by performing reasoning directly on continuous latent representations. This approach aims to enable test-time scaling and fine-grained control, overcoming limitations of existing methods.
papers.figure_caption: Test-time scaling. We investigate the effect of the number of latent during test-time. Under controlled experiments, LARC performs remarkable test-time scaling behavior , outperforming the best-of-N sampling on image generation [ 1 ] , image editing [ 27 ] , and visual reasoning [ 75 ] tasks.

papers.title: What Standard Evaluations Hide About Detectors of Hijacked LLM Agents: Rare Attacks, Unseen Tools and Benchmark Transfer
papers.abstract: This paper reveals that standard evaluations of LLM agent hijacking detectors are misleading due to their consistent, high attack rates and lack of diverse data. The core method involves testing existing detectors on benchmarks with varied attack rates and tool coverage, demonstrating that their performance significantly degrades when faced with rare attacks or unseen tools. The main contribution is highlighting the limitations of current evaluation practices and showing how detector effectiveness is overestimated, urging for more robust and realistic testing methodologies.

papers.title: Asynchronous Flow Map Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces asynchronous flow map language models (aFMLMs) to enable one-step parallel token prediction by incorporating an ordering. The core method learns "flow maps" that define a tokenwise time schedule, controlling denoising progress and internalizing this order into hidden computations. This allows for generating all tokens simultaneously in a single forward pass, a significant contribution for parallel language modeling.

papers.title: Completeness and Cost of Retrieval Structures for Multi-Tool Requests in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper investigates retrieval structures for LLM agents handling multi-tool requests, which often fail if even one required tool is missed. The authors compare six retrieval methods on multi-tool testbeds, measuring their ability to retrieve all necessary tools (completeness@k) and their associated computational costs. Their key contribution is demonstrating that existing retrieval methods perform poorly on multi-tool requests, especially those requiring many tools, and highlighting the need for specialized structures.

papers.title: How Much Can Tool Calls Reveal About You? Privacy Leakage from Tool-Call Traces
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the privacy risks associated with LLM agents interacting with external tools via tool-call traces. The authors introduce PrivacyTrace, a benchmark to study user-profile inference from these traces, finding that attackers can achieve a significant success rate in inferring user attributes. Their work highlights that tool arguments and returned results are key information sources, and cross-session trace linking amplifies this risk.
papers.figure_caption: Tool-call traces as a privacy side channel. In this example, geocoding results and patterns in requested travel times and transport modes may support inferences about the user’s location, health condition, and religious affiliation.

papers.title: Stepwise-Querying: Distilling Reasoning without Access to Teacher Chain-of-Thought
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Stepwise Querying, a method to distill reasoning from black-box large language models without direct access to their internal thought processes. By posing independent queries about intermediate steps, validity, and corrections, it generates richer supervision signals for training smaller student models. This approach significantly outperforms existing methods on mathematical and code reasoning tasks.

papers.title: AI evaluators favor job applications written by certain AI models, independent of candidate quality
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a framework to audit AI-driven job application screening. It reveals that AI evaluators exhibit a consistent preference for applications written by specific AI models, independent of the candidate's actual qualifications. This "generative preference hierarchy" can disadvantage certain models and introduce bias, with significant implications for fair hiring practices.

papers.title: AutoAnalysis: An automated, self-updating meta-analysis of human-AI collaboration
papers.abstract: This paper introduces AutoAnalysis, an automated system for continuously updating meta-analyses on human-AI collaboration. Its core method involves synthesizing empirical evidence to provide clear guidance on optimal human-AI teaming strategies. The key contribution is a dynamic, self-updating framework that addresses the limitations of manual meta-analyses, offering timely insights into when human-AI combinations outperform humans alone, but are generally outperformed by the superior individual agent.
